posts.title: 为什么他们必须觉得自己是对的
posts.excerpt: 你瘦了十斤，她说那是拍照角度。她不是在评价你，她是在记账——看懂那本账，你会少生很多气，也会知道哪些事你根本改不了。

posts.title: Why They Have to Be Right
posts.excerpt: You lost ten pounds; she says it's the camera angle. She isn't judging you — she's doing bookkeeping. Read the ledger and you'll waste a lot less anger.

posts.title: 我给儿子做了个「资产盘面」：83 条家规变成一个会涨跌的账本
posts.excerpt: 贴纸和小红花的问题不是不管用，是攒不住。我把家里那张 83 条的积分条例做成了一个像股票盘面的账本：走势线、历史新高、兑换商店、每笔可查的流水。这篇讲它长什么样、防哪些坑，以及代币制半个多世纪的研究证据和从多邻国、ClassDojo 抄来的几件事。

posts.title: I Built My Son an 'Asset Dashboard': 83 House Rules Turned into a Ledger That Goes Up and Down
posts.excerpt: The problem with stickers and gold stars isn't that they don't work — it's that they don't accumulate. I turned our family's 83-rule points chart into a stock-market-style ledger: a trend line, an all-time-high badge, a rewards shop, and an auditable transaction log. This post shows what it looks like, which loopholes it closes, plus half a century of token-economy research and what I borrowed from Duolingo and ClassDojo.

posts.title: 我给三年级的孩子做了个练习站：题目无限，但每一套都有头有尾
posts.excerpt: 一份期末卷长出来的练习站。一套 12 题、题号条、错题本记题型不记题目、经验值和勋章墙、每道题都能「再造一道类似的」。这篇把它有什么功能、长什么样、怎么用，一次讲清楚，配图全是真页面截的。

posts.title: 我给孩子做了个「资产盘面」，他每天自己去看涨了多少
posts.excerpt: 贴纸和小红花的问题不是不管用，是攒不住 —— 攒到第十七张就没人记得第一张是为什么给的。所以我把它做成了账本：每一笔加分扣分都有事由、有时间、有当时的余额，总数摆在最上面，像看盘一样。

posts.title: I Built My Kid His Own Market Dashboard, and He Checks It Every Day to See How Much He's Up
posts.excerpt: The problem with stickers and gold stars isn't that they don't work, it's that they don't add up — by the seventeenth one, nobody remembers what the first one was for. So I turned it into a ledger: every point earned or docked has a reason, a timestamp, and the balance at that moment, with the running total sitting up top, like watching a ticker.

posts.title: 我能出五万种题，孩子问我这套一共有几道
posts.excerpt: 一份三年级期末卷，我给孩子做了个练习站。五天里推翻了四次：无限流、错题重放、生成器当题库、全枚举炸库。每一次推翻的根因都一样——我把「技术上能做到」当成了「产品该长这样」。这篇把构建思路和使用方法一次写完。

posts.title: I Can Generate Fifty Thousand Questions. My Kid Asked How Many There Are.
posts.excerpt: One third-grade final exam, and a practice site I built for my kid. Four teardowns in five days: infinite stream, replaying wrong answers, mistaking generators for a question bank, and a combinatorial explosion. Every teardown had the same root cause—I kept treating 'technically possible' as 'this is what the product should be.' Here's the whole build, and how to use it.

posts.title: 我编了六个数，所有的门都是绿的
posts.excerpt: 把一张纸质规则表变成配置文件，最危险的动作不是算错，是在原文没给数的地方填一个看着合理的数。算错会被测试抓到；编的数不会——它和真的长得一模一样。

posts.title: I Invented Six Numbers, and Every Gate Was Green
posts.excerpt: Turning a paper rule sheet into a config file, the most dangerous move isn't getting the math wrong. It's filling in a plausible-looking number where the original gave none. Bad math gets caught by tests; invented numbers don't — they look exactly like the real ones.

posts.title: 我的检查器打了 102 个勾，你打开表是满屏错误
posts.excerpt: 我交表时附了一句「机器逐项核过，102 项全对」。对方打开，满屏错误。

posts.title: My Checker Gave 102 Green Ticks. You Opened the File to a Screen Full of Errors
posts.excerpt: I shipped the file with a note: machine-checked, 102 values verified. They opened it and every cell was broken. My checker was not lying — it was answering a different question than I thought.

posts.title: 我给自己装了 35 个报警器，最要紧的那个是我自己弄哑的
posts.excerpt: 为了让一个报警器少吵一点，我加了一行去重。它从此对这台机器上的所有对话永远沉默。

posts.title: I Keep 35 Alarms Watching Me. I Silenced the Most Important One Myself.
posts.excerpt: To make one alarm less noisy, I added a line that skipped repeats. From that moment it went permanently silent — for every conversation on this machine — and it still looked like it was running fine.

posts.title: 每次跑都有输出，所以没人发现它漏了 86%
posts.excerpt: 一个脚本跑了两个月，每次都有输出，每次看都正常。它漏掉了 86% 的短信。而这两个月里，我一直在拿它的输出做判断。

posts.title: It Printed Output Every Single Run — That's Why Nobody Noticed It Was Missing 86%
posts.excerpt: A script ran for two months. Every run produced output. Every output looked fine. It was missing 86% of my text messages — and I had been using that output to make decisions.

posts.title: CRITIC 客观赋权：它在奖励什么，什么时候会悄悄失效
posts.excerpt: CRITIC 号称让数据自己定权重，但它到底在奖励什么？用一个 5 企业 × 3 指标的完整算例拆开：权重 = 区分度 × 冲突性；同一份数据熵权抬的指标 CRITIC 反手砍掉。再给两个几乎没人提的失效条件——指标只剩 2 个时严格退化为标准差赋权，样本不够时权重是摆设。

posts.title: CRITIC Objective Weighting: What It Rewards, and When It Quietly Breaks
posts.excerpt: CRITIC claims to let the data set the weights — but what does it actually reward? A full worked example, plus two failure modes almost nobody mentions: with only 2 indicators it degenerates exactly to std-ratio weighting, and with too few samples the weights are decorative.

posts.title: 三个开源贡献复盘：Raycast · WeChatTweak · Cardinal

posts.title: Three Open-Source Contributions, In Retrospect: Raycast · WeChatTweak · Cardinal
